source.author: verg
source.text: Sic prior Aeneas; sequitur sic deinde Latinus suspiciens caelum tenditque ad sidera dextram:
source.text_original: Sic prior Aeneas; sequitur sic deinde Latinus / suspiciens caelum tenditque ad sidera dextram: /
source.text_english: Thus Aeneas spoke first; then Latinus followed, gazing up at the sky and stretching his right hand toward the stars:

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: laetus at impliciti Peleus rapit oscula nati suspiciensque polum placido si currere fluctu Pelea vultis ait ventosque optare ferentes, hoc, superi, servate caput.
reuse.text_original: laetus at impliciti Peleus rapit oscula nati / suspiciensque polum 'placido si currere fluctu / Pelea vultis' ait 'ventosque optare ferentes, / hoc, superi, servate caput.
reuse.text_english: Gladly, but Peleus, enfolding his son in his arms, snatches kisses from him and, looking up to heaven, says: if you wish Peleus to run on the calm wave and to desire favorable winds, then, gods above, preserve this head.
